# Where is Lingala commonly spoken in the Republic of the Congo?
Created from Britannica articles [using AI](https://www.britannica.com/about-britannica-ai). AI can make mistakes, so verify using Britannica articles. 
[ ![Congo \(Brazzaville\)](https://cdn.britannica.com/82/7182-050-B715705B/Flag-Republic-of-the-Congo.jpg?w=400&h=300&c=crop) ](https://cdn.britannica.com/82/7182-050-B715705B/Flag-Republic-of-the-Congo.jpg)
[Republic of the Congo](https://cdn.britannica.com/82/7182-050-B715705B/Flag-Republic-of-the-Congo.jpg) (more)
In the Republic of the Congo, [Lingala](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Lingala-language) is commonly spoken in the northern part of the country and within parts of the capital, [Brazzaville](https://www.britannica.com/place/Brazzaville).12
As a primary vernacular in the capital, it is closely associated with [urban culture](https://www.britannica.com/topic/urban-culture) and popular music. While [Kituba](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Kikongo-Kituba) serves as the trade language for the region between Brazzaville and the coast, Lingala remains the dominant trade language for areas north of the capital.21
